title: C++ Statements, Expressions and Blocks
learningObjectives: Explain the main concept of C++ Statements, Expressions and Blocks.
Identify the syntax or workflow elements involved.
Trace a small example and predict its result.
Apply the concept in a simple program or build task.

understand.concept: Expressions combine values, names and operators to produce a result or effect. Statements form complete instructions, while compound statements group instructions inside braces. A program's execution follows statement order unless a control-flow construct changes it.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding this topic helps you read, write, build and diagnose C++ programs instead of treating code as a black box.
understand.analogy: Imagine a well-organized workshop: each instruction has a place, tools are available when needed, and grouped tasks are kept together.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a learning aid; C++ syntax, compiler rules and execution semantics determine the actual behaviour.
understand.explain:
## Expressions
`3 + 4` is an expression that evaluates to a value. Assignments and function calls may also be expressions depending on their language rules.

## Simple statements
Declarations and many expression statements end with semicolons. Omitting a required semicolon is a common syntax error.

## Blocks
Braces group statements and create scope. Local names declared inside a block are generally not accessible outside that block. Nested blocks can be useful but should not be added without a reason.
